observations: The approved native frames are byte-identical to draft-05, and each was inspected again alongside the logical four-view sheet. They materially improve on the actual source slab: broad bulging irregular rock bodies, staggered exposed crowns, substantial side planes and two compact attached folded foliage clumps now establish a coherent rockery.

N/E/S/W retain consistent slate-blue/violet material, lighter crown planes and readable darker sides. Natural view occlusion varies which boulders and crevices are exposed; no facing has an unworked rear, dominant black dead face, clipped native silhouette or material artifact.

At logical scale on previously inspected light and dark backgrounds, the large facets and green folded accents remain clear without noisy detail. The former long straight column sidewalls and isolated spear/flap foliage are resolved to a satisfactory visible level.

The revised actual 390x844 phone edge and corner captures expose rock crowns and dark faces among separate crates, potted plants, barrels and lanterns. The cool rock/green rhythm contributes contiguous organic perimeter mass while warm accents remain distinct. This is a material consumer improvement over the plant-occluded draft captures.

Both primary default-camera captures and their individual screenshots were inspected. Supplemental +0.4-cell pan images were inspected separately and are correctly labeled; approval does not depend on substituting that pan for the default phone view.
The pale slab in the bottom decor comparison row remains the original reference prop. It was not counted as candidate rockery evidence.
remainingDifferences: The native result has simpler, quieter facet variation and compact foliage compared with the imagegen target. These differences are accepted because the broad rockery identity and phone-scale plane hierarchy are clear.
Exact target pixel silhouette, more frontal target camera and unseen-side target geometry are not reproduced; the frozen native source capture controls.
Small occluded leaf-tip peeks in E/S are visible enlarged but are not material defects at intended logical or phone size.
The phone viewport naturally crops the outermost perimeter at the screen edge; the exposed clusters and supplemental views provide sufficient consumer coverage.
